subject: reading
title: The Coin and the Hawk
about: Zack drops his duck-food coin in the hawk's pen and the hawk gives it back. Practises oi (coin), aw (hawk, claws), ou (proud), oo (zoo, swoops, good, oops) and ee (feed, see, feet) with ck words (Zack, ducks, picks), plus the tricky words go, to, one, they, from, my, you, are and says. Decodable at CKLA Unit 3, so he can read it alone.
tip: Cold read first, then read it to him, then let him read it again; ask him what he would feed the ducks with that coin.

passage.text:
Zack and Gran go to the zoo.
Zack has one coin to feed the ducks.

They see a big, proud hawk in a pen.
Zack looks in.
Oops!
The coin slips from his hand.
It drops in the pen.
Zack cannot get it.
"My coin!"

The hawk swoops down.
It picks up the coin in its claws.
Then it drops it at Zack's feet.
"You are a good hawk!" says Zack.

Zack and Gran feed the ducks.
Quack, quack!

cards.q: Who goes to the zoo with Zack?
cards.note: Zack and Gran go to the zoo.
The coin slips from his hand and drops in the pen.
Zack has one coin to feed the ducks.

cards.q: What does the hawk do with the coin?
cards.note: The hawk picks up the coin in its claws and drops it at Zack's feet.
First Zack and Gran go to the zoo; the coin drops after that.
Zack gets his coin back and they feed the ducks.

cards.q: How does Zack feel when the coin drops in the pen?
cards.note: Zack cannot get the coin and yells My coin!, so he is upset.

cards.q: Why does Zack say the hawk is good?
cards.note: The hawk brings the coin back, so Zack calls it a good hawk.
Claws are the sharp curved nails on a bird's feet; it grips with them.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: Coin is in the story; join and coil are look-alikes that are not.
